title: CI/CD federation: Azure vs AWS vs Google Cloud
summary: All three clouds trust GitHub's OIDC token instead of a stored secret. The idea is the same, but the place where the repo/environment check lives differs.

dimensions.label: Trust object
values: Federated identity credential on a UAMI or app registration
IAM OIDC provider + role trust policy

dimensions.label: Where the subject is checked
values: Provider attribute condition + principalSet on the SA binding

dimensions.label: Identity that gets the permissions
values: Service account (or the federated principal directly)

dimensions.label: Token exchange
values: STS token exchange, then SA impersonation

notes: The same failure mode exists everywhere: a subject check that is too broad, or missing. See the 'Broad federated subject' warning.
Only GCP has a two-level gate (pool condition, then SA binding). On Azure and AWS the single subject check carries all the weight.
